notes: `reports/VerificationTasks.pdf` section 10.1, Task 8: find a counterexample for `Q ⊆ Q↑` under the views `Va`, `Vb`, `Vc`. The schema, precondition and command are those of Example4036 (Task 7); only the direction of the containment differs.

The source documents the reformulations task document (sha256 `32a3ac6b428d851f0aaa4fb7acdbf2fe4ad5dacca93ee118837888ff91b7a1c6`) and `reports/VerificationTasks.pdf` (sha256 `796ff97c082c6fc70e75a60c0dd40ec0680b738d7184a8b8aefea8c681b3ebff`) carry the same section 10.1 text, so both name this task.

The command is not hand-authored: `Fidelity/Example4037.lean` states the PDF's Datalog programs, compiles each with `Datalog.WhielCompiler.Naive`, writes the two compiled commands one after the other, renames the generated snapshots `T_1`, `Q_1` and `QUp_1` to the auxiliary input names `T_aux`, `Q_aux` and `QUp_aux`, and proves the result equal to `inputCmd` by `decide +kernel`; the same module fixes `inputPre` as the three view equations and `inputPost` as the claim `Q ⊆ QUp`, and pins the single loop `Hoare.preprocess` computes from the sequence.

Verdict invalid, certified. The source paper's reformulation is only maximally contained in `Q`, so the reverse containment fails. The witness `F = {("b", "x", "d"), ("x", "y", "d")}` with `Vb = {("x", "d")}` and `Va = Vc = ∅` is the one `Fidelity/Example4037.lean` kernel-checks through `Hoare.CounterExample.kernelRefutes`: at exit `Q = {"x", "y"}` while `QUp = {"x"}`, so a two-hop route out of `"b"` on airline `"d"` refutes the triple. It was replayed through the Lean-owned `validate_counterexample` path, frozen as the durable record `Counterexample.json` (instance identity `3440c0ced55a518c0ae22fc8751223a3c05d404959fad4e70d6c03a1876fb0e0`, fuel consumed 12), and `Certificate/Invalid.lean` is rebuilt from exactly that record by `whiel-symbolic certificate build --counterexample`.

Reference encoding for intent only: `Benchmark/Example4037/Input.lean` on `origin/reformulation-multiview` at commit `7b793fe36c02d051a0771d110333d1c9bbca40cd`, an `IndexAlphaName` hand-written input in the earlier single-level framework. Nothing is copied from it.
The PDF's rule is `Q(y) :- T("b", y, u)` although its prose says the airports reachable "from a"; the rule is encoded literally, with the constant "b".

`Counterexample.json` was re-frozen with this header-corrected input's source and scope identities while preserving the canonical instance, provenance, Lean-issued instance identity `3440c0ced55a518c0ae22fc8751223a3c05d404959fad4e70d6c03a1876fb0e0`, structural replay policy, and fuel consumed 12. `Certificate/Invalid.lean` is regenerated from exactly that durable record, uses only `programInst![…]` for the instance, omits the former `counterExampleRows` and `counterExampleInput_eq_keyedRows` declarations, and revalidates at exactly propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound.
title: Airline reachability query versus its three-view reformulation, reverse containment
explanation: This case uses the same global and local programs, views, and precondition as Example4036 (per-airline reachability T restricted to departures from "b" for Q, versus the three-view reformulation QUp), but tests the opposite direction of containment, Q ⊆ QUp: that every airport genuinely reachable from "b" on a single airline is also captured by the reformulation. This claim is invalid, certified by a kernel-checked counterexample: the reformulation is only maximally (forward-) contained in Q, not surjective onto it, so a two-hop route out of "b" on an airline other than "a" or "c" is invisible to all three views. The witness is F = {("b","x","d"), ("x","y","d")}, where at exit Q = {"x","y"} but QUp = {"x"}.
preInWords: The precondition states the same three view equations as Example4036: Va is F restricted to airline "a", Vb is F restricted to flights departing "b", and Vc is the two-hop composition of two airline-"c" flights.
postInWords: The postcondition asserts Q ⊆ QUp, that every airport genuinely reachable from "b" on one airline is captured by the reformulation — a claim that fails.
